sentences.text: Duntroonornis parvus, or the Duntroon penguin, was an extinct bird that lived in New Zealand during the Late Oligocene. This species was relatively small, comparable in size to the modern Fiordland crested penguin. The specific epithet parvus is Latin for "small", highlighting its diminutive stature.
Taxonomically, the animal is classified within the order Sphenisciformes and the family Spheniscidae.
Brian Marples described the species in 1952 based on a left tarsometatarsus fossil found near Duntroon in the Kokoamu Greensand Formation. The genus name Duntroonornis translates to "Duntroon bird".
Fossils discovered in the Hakataramea Valley might also belong to this species.
The fossil record for Duntroonornis spans the Chattian stage of the Late Oligocene, between 27.3 and 25.2 million years ago.
